metadata.scope: OSINT research on 5 Canadian MPs — lobbying contacts, MAID votes, controversies, foreign connections
metadata.methodology: Public web sources: OpenParliament, CBC, Globe and Mail, lobbycanada.gc.ca, ourcommons.ca, Wikipedia, Hill Times, Global News, CTV News, B'nai Brith Canada

mps.name: Sean Casey
mps.current_role: MP for Charlottetown (elected 2011, re-elected 2015, 2019, 2021, 2025). Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Veterans Affairs and Associate Minister of National Defence (June 2025-present). Chair of the Standing Committee on Human Resources, Skills and Social Development and the Status of Persons with Disabilities. Member of the Standing Committee on Veterans Affairs. Previously served as Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Fisheries, Oceans and the Canadian Coast Guard; Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada; and Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Canadian Heritage.

controversies.title: Criticism of Trudeau over Freeland resignation handling
controversies.detail: In December 2024, Casey publicly called on PM Trudeau to resign following the resignation of Finance Minister Chrystia Freeland. He criticized how Trudeau handled Freeland's departure and urged the PM to stop the public campaign against Freeland. Casey was among the Liberal MPs who broke ranks during the 2024-2025 Canadian political crisis.

controversies.title: Former registered lobbyist before entering Parliament
controversies.detail: Prior to his election, Casey was a lawyer and businessman who also held registrations in the Federal Lobbying Registry as a consultant lobbyist. Records show registrations for clients including 'ole' (registration starting December 22, 2016) and the Beaverbrook Art Gallery (registration starting November 13, 2020). He was also president of the Paderno Group of Companies from 2003 to 2008.

lobbying_highlights: 439 registered lobbying contacts in the Federal Lobbyists Registration System
Casey himself held consultant lobbyist registrations (for 'ole' and the Beaverbrook Art Gallery) before entering Parliament
As a senior Parliamentary Secretary across multiple portfolios (Justice, Fisheries, Heritage, Veterans Affairs), he is a high-value target for lobbyists across diverse policy sectors
Listed in lobbycanada.gc.ca with contacts spanning multiple sectors
mps.maid_position: Voted YES on Bill C-14 (2016, original MAID legislation) and YES on Bill C-7 (2021, MAID expansion removing the 'reasonably foreseeable natural death' requirement). Consistent supporter of MAID as government policy.
foreign_connections: No documented foreign government connections or ethics investigations found in public records
Endorsed Chrystia Freeland in the 2025 Liberal Party leadership election
financial_notes: Holds a nominal interest in Other Ocean Partners North ULC, a holding company that owns a rental property in Cornwall, PEI (disclosed via Office of the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner)
Beneficiary of the Sean J. Casey Family Trust, which has interests in private corporations
Former partner at Stewart McKelvey law firm (1993-2003), managing partner (2008-2011)
Former president of Paderno Group of Companies (2003-2008)
No ethics commissioner investigations or violations found in public records

mps.name: Salma Zahid
mps.current_role: MP for Scarborough Centre--Don Valley East (originally elected for Scarborough Centre in 2015, re-elected 2019, 2021; won redistributed riding in 2025 with 57% of vote). Chair of the Canada-Palestine Parliamentary Friendship Group. Member of the Standing Committees on Public Safety and Citizenship and Immigration. Cancer survivor (Stage 4 Non-Hodgkin lymphoma, 2018, now in remission).

controversies.title: Holocaust denial event at Parliament Hill (November 2022)
controversies.detail: Zahid, as chair of the Canada-Palestine Parliamentary Friendship Group, hosted a Parliament Hill reception for the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People at which Nazih Khatatba, publisher of the Arabic-language newspaper Meshwar Media, attended. Conservative MP Melissa Lantsman called Khatatba 'a dangerous anti-Semite, Holocaust denier, and terrorist sympathizer.' Zahid stated Khatatba was not invited by name but responded to an open invitation distributed by the Canadian Palestinian Organizations Coalition. B'nai Brith Canada and CIJA condemned his attendance. Zahid issued a statement against antisemitism but did not publicly distance herself or the Friendship Group from Khatatba or Meshwar Media. In 2019, Zahid had agreed to stop advertising in Meshwar Media after being notified of its content by B'nai Brith, and Khatatba participated in a 2020 Zoom call hosted by Zahid.

controversies.title: Threat to resign parliamentary committee duties over Gaza (July 2024)
controversies.detail: Zahid quietly threatened to quit her parliamentary committee duties in protest over the Liberal government's handling of the Israel-Gaza conflict. Her draft statement criticized the government for not treating 'Islamophobia and anti-Palestinian racism with the seriousness that it deserves.' She demanded Canada recognize a Palestinian state and take steps to prevent conflict from spilling into Lebanon. She never publicly released the statement and never resigned from her committee positions.

controversies.title: Anti-Palestinian racism roundtable (July 2024)
controversies.detail: Co-hosted a roundtable with MP Sameer Zuberi in Toronto about anti-Palestinian racism, pushing for it to be included in the federal government's updated anti-racism strategy. Among the most vocal pro-Palestinian voices in the Liberal caucus since October 2023; one of the first Liberal MPs to call for a ceasefire in the Middle East conflict.

controversies.title: Support for South Africa ICJ genocide case against Israel (January 2024)
controversies.detail: Called on colleagues in the House of Commons to support South Africa's application to prosecute Israel for genocide at the International Court of Justice, breaking with the standard Liberal and historical Canadian position of political support for Israel.

lobbying_highlights: 431 registered lobbying contacts in the Federal Lobbyists Registration System
As chair of the Canada-Palestine Parliamentary Friendship Group, she is a focal point for lobbying from Middle East policy organizations on both sides
Member of Public Safety and Citizenship and Immigration committees, attracting lobbying from security and immigration sectors
mps.maid_position: Voted YES on Bill C-14 (2016, original MAID legislation) and YES on Bill C-7 (2021, MAID expansion removing the 'reasonably foreseeable natural death' requirement). Consistent supporter of MAID as government policy.
foreign_connections: Chair of the Canada-Palestine Parliamentary Friendship Group — significant advocacy for Palestinian statehood and criticism of Israeli government actions

mps.name: Peter Fragiskatos
mps.current_role: MP for London Centre (elected 2015 for London North Centre, re-elected 2019, 2021, 2025 with 57% of the vote). Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship (June 2025-present). Former professor of political science at Huron University College and King's University College (University of Western Ontario). PhD in international relations from the University of Cambridge.

controversies.title: Office vandalized during pro-Palestine protests (October-November 2023)
controversies.detail: Fragiskatos' downtown London office was vandalized twice in three weeks. On October 22, 2023, protesters sprayed ketchup on windows and doors to simulate blood during a rally calling for a ceasefire in Gaza. A second act of vandalism with paint occurred in November 2023. Dr. Tarek Loubani, a Western University professor, was charged with mischief for the ketchup incident, but the Crown withdrew the charge. Hours after charges were dropped, Loubani returned to Fragiskatos' office in renewed protest. Fragiskatos had issued a statement on October 15 condemning Hamas as a terrorist organization, affirming Israel's right to self-defence, and calling for humanitarian aid to Gaza civilians.

controversies.title: Called on Trudeau to resign (January 2025)
controversies.detail: Fragiskatos joined the chorus of Liberal MPs publicly calling on PM Trudeau to resign during the 2024-2025 Canadian political crisis, stating that 'the continued leadership of Prime Minister Trudeau is just not tenable -- in particular of what's happened with Chrystia Freeland.'

mps.maid_position: Voted YES on Bill C-14 (2016, original MAID legislation) and YES on Bill C-7 (2021, MAID expansion removing the 'reasonably foreseeable natural death' requirement). Consistent supporter of MAID as government policy.

mps.name: Sonia Sidhu
mps.current_role: MP for Brampton South (elected 2015, re-elected 2019, 2021, 2025 with 49% of the vote). Vice-Chair of the Standing Committee on the Status of Women. Chair and Liberal caucus champion for the All-Party Diabetes Caucus. Member of the Standing Committee on Health. General-Secretary of the Canada-India Parliamentary Friendship Group. Executive member of the Canada-Poland and Canada-Portugal Parliamentary Friendship Groups. Author of Bill C-237 (National Framework for Diabetes Act, passed Senate June 2021).

controversies.title: Brampton Hindu temple protest response (November 2024)
controversies.detail: Amid escalating Canada-India tensions over alleged Khalistani extremism and Indian government interference, Sidhu publicly condemned violence at a Brampton Hindu temple in November 2024. She criticized protests at places of worship by both pro-India and pro-Khalistan groups. She also spoke in the House regarding RCMP allegations concerning foreign interference from the Government of India, noting RCMP evidence linking Indian government agents to homicides and violence in Canada.

controversies.title: Campaign sign vandalism (2019 election)
controversies.detail: During the 2019 federal election campaign, Sidhu reported hundreds of her lawn signs were stolen or vandalized in Brampton South, contributing to broader tensions among candidates in the riding. No perpetrators were publicly identified or charged.

mps.name: Ali Ehsassi
mps.current_role: MP for Willowdale (elected 2015, re-elected 2019, 2021, 2025). Parliamentary Secretary to the President of the King's Privy Council for Canada and Minister responsible for Canada-U.S. trade matters (May 2025-present). Briefly served as Minister of Government Transformation, Public Services and Procurement (March 14 - May 13, 2025) in Mark Carney's 30th Canadian Ministry. Chair of the Standing Committee on Foreign Affairs and International Development (since June 2022). Chair of the All-Party Parliamentary Group for the Prevention of Genocide and Other Crimes Against Humanity. Co-Chair of the 416 Caucus.

controversies.title: Stephane Dion Iran roundtable guest list controversy (October 2016)
controversies.detail: Ehsassi and fellow MP Majid Jowhari organized a roundtable with Foreign Affairs Minister Stephane Dion at Toronto's Westin Prince hotel with approximately 60 Iranian Canadians. The event drew criticism because most of those invited had signed a petition to re-open the Canadian embassy in Iran, leading to accusations that the guest list was stacked in favor of re-engagement with the Iranian regime. Ehsassi rejected the accusation, stating he wanted 'anyone who has a strong opinion' to attend and had invited Baha'i community members (a persecuted minority in Iran) who were unable to attend.

controversies.title: Family ties to Iranian Pahlavi dynasty
controversies.detail: Ehsassi's maternal great-grandfather was Abdolhossein Teymourtash, the first Minister of Court during the Pahlavi dynasty in Iran. His father was an Iranian diplomat who worked in Iran's embassy in Switzerland when Ehsassi was born. While Ehsassi has been a vocal critic of the current Iranian regime, his family's historical connections to the previous Iranian government have been noted. His family left Iran during the Iranian Revolution.
